comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4-C6, C28-C31, C35, C41, C46-C48 regarding selection patterns across env regions. Both evaluations find the evidence for temporal and magnitude hierarchy of selection pressures to be well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes statistical validation and quantitative comparisons, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the findings about shared selection patterns and stronger selection for autologous antibodies versus bnAbs.

Strong agreement on claims C7, C60, C73, C95 regarding similarity of selection coefficients between humans and macaques. Both evaluations highlight the compelling quantitative evidence (r>0.95, p<10^-20). OpenEval notes C90 (correlation extends to shuffled sequences) which peer reviewers don't explicitly address, but peer reviewers emphasize the broader significance for establishing shared evolutionary patterns.

Divergent evaluations on claims C8, C61-C63, C69-C72 regarding fitness gains preceding bnAb emergence. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on temporal analysis and exclusion of resistance mutations as drivers. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting that 'bNAb detection is different from bNAb presence' and that the causal interpretation, while plausible, remains incompletely established. OpenEval includes C63 which peer review doesn't explicitly address.

Perfect agreement on claims C66-C67 regarding modest epistatic interactions and validation of the additive model. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes the high correlation (r~0.85-0.95) between model types, while peer reviewers praise the mathematical approach (Equation 3) as 'beautiful and intuitive.'

Agreement on claims C83-C86 regarding methodological limitations and alternative explanations. Both evaluations support the authors' transparent acknowledgment of limitations while finding the main interpretation plausible. OpenEval emphasizes evidence from RM5695 (C86) arguing against alternative explanations, which peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of a 'coherent and compelling picture.'

Partial overlap on macaque data claims. OpenEval addresses C49-C50, C57-C58 (weak frequency-fitness association, VL-enhancing mutations), rating as SUPPORTED. Peer R4 addresses a broader set including C49-C50, C57-C58, C63-C65, C76-C82 (selection coefficients, resistance mutations), also rating as SUPPORTED. Both agree on compatibility of human and macaque selection coefficients.

OpenEval R7 addresses claims C76-C80, C82 regarding quantitative selection coefficients for resistance mutations, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer R4 includes these claims (C76-C82) within a broader evaluation that also covers C49-C50, C57-C58, C63-C65. Both evaluations support the findings about selection being larger for autologous antibodies than bnAbs.

OpenEval R5 addresses claims C64-C65 regarding RM6072 as an informative outlier case with T234N mutation, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer R4 includes C64-C65 within a broader evaluation covering multiple macaque-related claims (C49-C50, C57-C58, C63-C65, C76-C82), also rating as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on claims C88-C89 regarding comparison with LASSIE method. OpenEval explicitly addresses the methodological comparison showing partial agreement and validation. Peer R7 includes C87-C89 and implicitly supports the comparison by praising the MPL approach as 'a valuable introduction to a practical method,' though doesn't explicitly discuss the LASSIE comparison details.

Partial overlap on claims C91-C94 regarding weak frequency-fitness relationship and mutational biases. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with explicit reference to Figure 4-supplement 1. Peer R8 addresses C90-C98 more broadly, supporting the general patterns of positive selection and evolutionary constraints, confirming that hypervariability results from immune evasion rather than neutral evolution.

OpenEval R13 addresses claim C97 regarding predictability of evolution on short time scales, rating as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about limited sample size. Peer R8 includes C97 within a broader evaluation (C90-C98) supporting the implications about evolutionary predictability and constraints, affirming interest to the quantitative evolution community.

OpenEval R11 addresses claims C74, C96 regarding future work on engineered immunogens and neutral paths, rating as UNCERTAIN since these are speculative hypotheses without experimental validation. Peer R8 includes C96 within a broader evaluation (C90-C98) that supports the general implications, but doesn't specifically distinguish speculative future directions from established findings.

OpenEval R12 addresses claims C1-C3, C9-C25, C75, C81, C84, C87, C94, C98 representing background knowledge and prior work, rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review result specifically evaluates these foundational/contextual claims, as peer reviewers focus on novel findings rather than cataloging cited background literature.

Minor overlap on claim C90. OpenEval R2 includes C90 (correlation extends to shuffled sequences) as part of evidence for human-macaque similarity, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 includes C90 within broader evaluation (C90-C98) about evolutionary patterns and predictability, also rating as SUPPORTED, though doesn't specifically discuss the shuffled sequence analysis.

Minimal overlap on claim C63. OpenEval R3 includes C63 (exclusion of bnAb resistance mutations as drivers of fitness gains) as supporting evidence for the temporal relationship between fitness gains and bnAb emergence. Peer R4 includes C63 within a broader evaluation of macaque data findings, both rating their respective claim sets as SUPPORTED.
